items.title: SK하이닉스, 안전·보안 국제 인증으로 피지컬 AI 메모리 신뢰성 강화

items.title: 삼성바이오, 유증 우리사주·구주주 청약률 96.83%…2.6조 M&A 조달 순항

items.title: 카카오, 정신아·김도영 해외 IR 나서…인적분할 설득 총력
items.snippet: 카카오가 인적분할을 앞두고 해외 기관투자자들을 직접 만나 분할 취지와 성장 전략을 설명하는 등 투자자 설득에 나섰다.인적분할 이후 사업별 성장 전략에 대한 시장의 이해를 높이는 동시에 기업가치 재평가를 위한 투자자 기반을 확보하려는 행보로 풀이된다.11일 카카오에 따르면 정신아 카카오 대표와 김도영 카카오X 대표 내정자는 이날부터 12일까지 홍콩과 싱가포르에서 해외 투자자 및 기관 10여 곳을 대상으로 기업설명회(IR)를 진행한다.이번 IR에서는 인적분할의 배경과 목적을 설명하고 분할 이후 카카오AI와 카카오X의 사업 전략과 중장

items.title: AP시스템, 반도체 부문 신규 수주 1000억원 돌파
items.snippet: 에이피시스템(AP시스템)이 올해 반도체 부문 신규 수주가 이달 기준 1000억원을 돌파했다고 10일 밝혔다. 지난해 반도체 부문 매출(652억원)의 1.5배 수준이다. 매출은 2027년까지 나눠 인식된다.핵심 기술인 급속열처리(RTP) 장비 수주가 늘어난 덕이다. items.title: 딥엑스, 삼성 2나노 칩 'DX-M2' 마스크 제작 착수...내년 4분기 양산

items.title: 파네시아, 미주법인 설립...마이크로소프트 출신 총괄대표 영입
items.snippet: 인공지능(AI) 인프라 연결 솔루션 개발기업 파네시아가 미주법인을 설립하고 총괄대표를 영입했다고 10일 밝혔다.신규 미주법인 총괄대표는 엘리스 윌슨 전 마이크로소프트(MS) 수석 소프트웨어 엔지니어 매니저다. items.title: KIND, 아일랜드 에너지저장장치 인프라 공동 개발 나서
items.snippet: 한국해외인프라도시개발지원공사(KIND)는 아일랜드 에너지저장장치 사업의 공동 개발 및 국내 기업의 해외 인프라사업 공동 진출을 위한 업무협약을 체결했다고 11일 밝혔다.KIND는 업무협약을 체결한 신한자산운용과 효성중공업, 아일랜드 럼클룬 에너지와 에너지저장장치(BESS) 사업의 개발 및 투자 협력 체계를 구축한다.협약 대상 사업은 아일랜드 골웨이 카운티 쿨포우라 일대에서 추진되는 에너지저장장치 사업이다. 풍력 등 재생에너지 발전량을 안정화하고, 전력 수급 유연성 등을 제고한다는 계획이다.관계사들은 대규모 에너지저장장치의 안정적인

items.title: 딥엑스, 2026 특허기술상 ‘홍대용상’ 수상…AI반도체 원천기술 인정

items.title: 삼성전자가 키우면 다르다…투자자가 주목하는 'C랩 스타트업'
items.snippet: 엄마의 스마트폰으로 아이의 숨소리를 진단하는 회사, 로봇이 배울 교과서를 만드는 회사. 삼성전자가 골라 키운 스타트업들이 현재까지 확보한 투자금은 2조2천억원에 달한다. items.title: EVG, 첨단 본딩 기술로 양자컴퓨팅 개발 지원
items.snippet: 반도체 장비업체 EV그룹(EVG)이 본딩 등 첨단 패키징 기술을 활용해 양자컴퓨팅 개발을 지원한다고 10일 밝혔다. 이온 트랩, 초전도, 광자, 스핀 등 다양한 방식으로 제조하는 양자 칩에 이종 소재와 소자를 집적해 큐비트 수를 늘릴 수 있도록 돕는다.실리콘 오스트리아 랩스(SAL)의 전략적 파트너로 참여하고 있다. items.title: 퀄리타스반도체, 모빌린트 로봇용 SoC에 통합 솔루션 공급
items.snippet: 반도체 설계자산(IP) 기업 퀄리타스반도체가 모빌린트에 초고속 데이터 통신 규격(인터페이스) IP 통합 솔루션을 공급한다고 10일 밝혔다.해당 솔루션은 PCI익스프레스(PCIe) 서브시스템, 모바일·임베디드용 영상 인터페이스(MIPI) 서브시스템, 칩렛용 상호연결(인터커넥트) 기술 등이 포함된다. 모빌린트는 공급받은 솔루션으로 고성능 신경망처리장치(NPU) 기반 시스템온칩(SoC)을 개발한다. 로봇, 자율주행차 등 피지컬 AI용 SoC다. 모빌린트는 지난달 휴머노이드용 AI 연산 플랫폼을 개발한다고 밝힌 바 있다.PCIe 서브시스템

items.title: 호남권 반도체 전력공급선로 내년 1월 착공
items.snippet: 호남권 반도체에 전력을 적기에 공급하기 위한 전력공급선로 공사가 내년 1월 시작된다.기후에너지환경부는 김성환 장관이 11일 호남권 반도체 산단 전력공급선로 경과지에서 한국전력공사로부터 공급선로 건설 계획과 현장 공사 여건을 보고받는다고 밝혔다.전력공급선로는 지난 8월 호남권 메가프로젝트 전력공급 협약 체결에 이어 9월 국무회의에서 구체적인 건설 계획이 의결됐다.이후 예비타당성조사(예타) 면제가 확정돼 설계 용역을 발주 중이며 내년 1월 수직구 착공을 시작으로 건설에 들어갈 예정이다.김 장관은 전남광주 서구에 있는 변전소 후보지도

items.title: 무신사, 단체복 비즈니스 시장 진출…'무신사 유니폼' 출시
items.snippet: 무신사가 기업·기관 등 단체 고객의 맞춤형 유니폼을 제작해주는 단체복 비즈니스 시장에 진출한다.무신사는 이를 위해 B2B(기업 간 거래) 서비스 전용 플랫폼 '무신사 유니폼'(MUSINSA UNIFORM)을 지난 10일 출시했다고 11일 밝혔다.무신사 유니폼은 기업·기관·동호회 등 단체복을 대량 구매하는 고객이 상품 선택부터 견적, 주문까지 한 번에 진행할 수 있는 온라인 전용 플랫폼이다.B2B 고객은 무신사 유니폼 서비스를 통해 무신사 스탠다드, 무신사 스탠다드 스포츠, 챔피온 중에서 희망 브랜드를 고를 수 있다.무신사는 향후

items.title: 코스피, 美연준 '빅스텝'우려에 약보합…코스닥은 2% 가까이 상승
items.snippet: 코스피가 미국의 기준금리 인상 우려와 뉴욕증시 약세 여파로 하락 출발했다. 반면 코스닥은 이차전지와 반도체 장비, 바이오 종목을 중심으로 매수세가 유입되며 2% 가까이 상승하고 있다.11일 개장 초반 코스피는 전 거래일보다 13.61포인트(0.26%) 내린 5,225.52에 거래되고 있다.전날 4.39% 급등하며 4거래일 만에 반등에 성공했던 코스피는 하루 만에 다시 하락 압력을 받고 있다.간밤 미국의 10월 소비자물가지수(CPI)가 시장 예상치를 웃돌면서 연방준비제도(Fed·연준)의 긴축 강화 가능성이 부각된 영향으로 풀이된다.

items.title: ‘퇴사 뒤 재입사’ 꼼수… 의사부부 등 부정청약 354건 적발
items.snippet: 고소득 의사 부부인 A 씨와 B 씨는 서울 아파트 입주자 모집공고 직전에 다니던 병원에서 퇴사했다. 공고일 당시에는 다른 병원에서 일용직으로 근무했고, 공고 직후에는 기존 병원에 재입사했다. 부부는 이 방법으로 소득을 낮춰 신혼부부 특별공급 소득우선 물량에 당첨됐다. 국토교통부는 이들이 청약자의 소득을 공고일 기준으로 산정한다는 점을 노리고 ‘위장퇴사’한 것으로 보고 수사 의뢰하기로 했다. 국토부와 국무조정실 부동산감독추진단은 지난해 7월부터 올해 3월까지 분양한 주요 단지 43곳, 2만5000채의 당첨자 등을 집중 점검해 이 같은 부정청약 의심 사례 354건을 적발했다고 10일 밝혔다. 정부는 이들 모두를 수사 의뢰할 예정이다. 적발 사례 중에는 청약 자격을 얻거나 부양가족 수를 부풀리려 주소만 옮긴 위장전입이 334건으로 가장 많았다. 유...

items.title: ‘재개발 알박기’ 지적했던 李 “불법행위 방치 전수조사하라”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 10일 재개발 구역 ‘알박기’를 거론하면서 전국의 불법행위 방치 실태를 전수 조사하라고 지시했다. 단순 계도 차원을 넘어 범정부 차원의 강력한 수사와 처벌을 통해 부동산 불법행위를 근절해야 한다는 의지를 드러낸 것. 법 집행을 무력화하고 이익을 얻는 관행을 바로잡아 법치주의를 확립하겠다는 국정 기조를 재차 강조한 것으로 풀이된다. 이 대통령은 10일 청와대에서 열린 국무회의에서 “우리 사회 곳곳에 자리한 각종 범죄, 비리, 불공정에 대한 대응에 범정부적인 역량을 집중해야 되겠다. 무엇보다 중요한 건 문제가 발생한 후에 사후약방문식으로 수습하는 데 그치지 않는 것”이라며 “아예 이들 범죄가 우리 사회에 발을 붙일 수조차 없도록 촘촘하고 빈틈없는 대응 체계를 구축해야 한다. 관계 당국은 각 부처청 간에 불필요한 칸막이를 허물고 모...

items.title: ‘청해부대 호르무즈 인근 작전’ 국무회의 의결 …이란 “파병 자제해야” 韓 “전쟁 개입 없을것”
items.snippet: 청해부대의 작전구역을 아덴만에서 오만 남방 외해까지 약 2배로 넓히고 기뢰 제거 전력을 증파하는 파견 연장 동의안이 10일 국무회의를 통과해 국회에 제출됐다. 이에 따라 동의안 처리의 공은 국회로 넘어갔다. 범여권 진보 진영에서 호르무즈 ‘우회 파병’이란 비판이 나오는 가운데, 정부는 ‘전쟁 불개입 원칙’을 거듭 강조했다. 국방부는 이날 이재명 대통령 주재로 열린 국무회의에서 이 같은 내용의 동의안이 의결된 뒤 국회에 제출됐다고 밝혔다. 국회 국방위원회 심사와 본회의 표결을 거쳐 동의안이 통과되면 파견 기간은 내년 12월 31일까지 연장된다. 조국혁신당과 진보당은 이번 동의안이 ‘사실상 호르무즈 파병’이라며 반대하고 있다. 조국혁신당 김준형 원내대표는 5일 “직접적인 전투에 참여하지 않는다고 해서 전쟁 개입의 위험이 사라지는 것은 아니다”라며...

items.title: 캠벨 “트럼프, 시진핑에 북미대화 도움 요청”… 김정은 방중 촉각
items.snippet: 중국 선전 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의가 일주일 앞으로 다가오면서 한반도 정세가 분수령을 맞고 있다는 분석이 나온다. 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석이 북-미 정상회담 중재에 나선 것으로 알려진 가운데, 정부는 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 방중 여부에 촉각을 곤두세우고 있다. APEC 정상회의를 계기로 추진되는 미중, 미-중-러 정상회담에서도 한반도 문제가 의제가 될 것으로 알려진 만큼 APEC 정상회의를 기점으로 주요국의 움직임이 활발해질 수 있다는 관측이 나온다. ● APEC 앞두고 북-미 중재 나선 시진핑 9일(현지 시간) 커트 캠벨 전 미국 국무부 부장관은 아시아태평양 지역 언론인 간담회에서 “도널드 트럼프 대통령이 시 주석에게 북-미 대화가 성사되도록 도움을 요청한 것으로 알고 있다”고 말했다. items.title: 스틸 “美기업, 한국서 공정경쟁 할 수 있어야”…조셉 윤 “전작권 전환, 한미동맹 약화 불가피”
items.snippet: 미셸 스틸 주한 미국대사가 10일 “약속한 대로 한국에 진출한 미국 기업이 공정한 환경에서 경쟁할 수 있어야 한다”고 말했다. 전날(9일) 공정거래위원회가 쿠팡에 3008억 원의 과징금 부과를 결정한 직후 다시 미국 기업에 대한 ‘공정한 대우’를 강조한 것. 조셉 윤 전 주한 미국대사대리는 “한미동맹의 약화 없이 전시작전통제권(전작권) 전환은 불가능하다”면서 전작권 전환이 빠르게 진전되기 어려울 것으로 전망했다. 스틸 대사는 이날 국회 한미의원연맹이 주최한 한미외교포럼에서 “안보 없이 번영을 누릴 수 없으며 번영 없이 실질적으로 안보를 강화할 수 없다”면서 이같이 말했다. 그는 지난달 21일 주한미국상공회의소(암참) 개최 특별 오찬간담회에서도 한국 진출 미국 기업에 대한 “공정한 조건”을 강조한 바 있다. 스틸 대사는 한미 정상 간 합의에 따...

items.title: 李 “한미 외교안보 합의 이행” 전작권-핵잠 계속 추진 강조
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 10일 미국 중간선거 결과와 관련해 “양국이 외교·안보 분야에서 합의한 사항들이 제대로 이행될 수 있도록 지혜를 모아가야겠다”고 밝혔다. 미국 민주당이 상·하원을 장악한 ‘블루 쓰나미(Blue Tsunami·민주당의 압승)’로 전시작전통제권 전환과 핵추진잠수함 도입 등에 속도를 내기 어려울 수 있다는 우려가 나오자 합의사항 이행을 강조한 것으로 풀이된다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 “무엇보다 중요한 것은 한미가 상호 호혜적인 관점에서 양국 간에 신뢰와 협력의 기반을 다지고 넓히는 데 외교력을 집중하는 것”이라며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “미국 행정부와 긴밀한 협조를 이어가는 동시에 미 의회 내에도 초당적인 협력 토대를 구축하고 각 주 정부들과 경제계 등으로 소통의 폭을 넓혀 가야겠다”고 했다. 그러면서 “정부...

items.title: 김정관 “호남 반도체 팹 배치 이달내 마무리”
items.snippet: 김정관 산업통상부 장관이 10일 호남 반도체 클러스터 팹(반도체 생산라인) 배치와 관련해 “이번 달 안에 마무리될 예정”이라고 밝혔다. 김 장관은 이날 국회에서 열린 예산결산특별위원회 전체회의에서 더불어민주당 조인철 의원이 향후 일정에 대해 묻자 “기업들이 팹 배치를 어떻게 하느냐가 굉장히 중요한 상황”이라며 이같이 밝혔다. 그는 “(팹 배치는) 모든 것의 일종의 출발점이라고 볼 수 있을 것 같다”며 “여기에 따라서 이제 산단 협약도 진행이 될 거라고 예상된다”고 했다. 호남 반도체 클러스터 부지에 위치한 광주 군 공항 이전에 대해서는 “금년 말, 2027년 정도에 전체적인 윤곽이 나타날 거라고 본다”며 “공항 이전 전이라도 일부 지역에서는 공사가 가능하다는 판단이 있어서 그 지역에 대한 공사를 지금 검토하고 있다”고 했다. 기업들의 투자 철...

items.title: 이형일 “종부세 실거주 우대” 수정 선그어…李대통령, 오늘 與 김민석-한병도와 만찬
items.snippet: 이형일 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관이 “거주용 주택에 대한 우대 원칙은 지켜져야 한다”며 비거주 1주택자의 종합부동산세(종부세) 기본공제 완화에 선을 그었다. 하지만 더불어민주당 수도권 의원들은 “정부와 지속적으로 협의할 것”이라며 부동산 세제 완화 필요성을 재차 강조했다. 이 부총리는 10일 국회 예산결산특별위원회 전체회의에서 “이번 세제 개편의 핵심은 거주 중심의 주택시장을 정착시키자는 것”이라며 이같이 말했다. 최근 민주당 내에서 비거주 1주택자의 종부세 기본공제액을 실거주 1주택자와 동일한 14억 원으로 상향해야 한다는 요구가 잇따르자 정부의 기존 원칙을 재확인한 것이다. 이 부총리는 이날 X(옛 트위터)에도 글을 올려 “주택이 한정된 상황에서 실제 거주하려는 국민께 소유 기회가 최대한 주어지려면 정부의 원칙이 지켜져야 한다”고 재차 강...

items.title: 與 “주가 누르기 방지법 내달초까지 처리”… 재계 “시장 혼란”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 상속·증여세를 줄이려고 주가를 일부러 낮추는 것을 막는 이른바 ‘주가 누르기 방지법’(상속·증여세법 개정안)을 다음 달 초까지 처리하기로 했다. 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF) 논란과 증시 하락 국면 속에 주가 부양을 위한 입법 드라이브에 나선 것. 다만 재계는 물론이고 여당 내에서도 “시장에 큰 혼란을 불러올 수 있다”는 우려가 나오고 있다. 민주당 김성회 원내대변인은 10일 의총 뒤 기자들과 만나 “상속·증여세법은 세법인 만큼 정기국회 안에 처리한다”고 밝혔다. 정부는 당초 6년 6개월(13개 반기) 중 6년 이상 주가순자산비율(PBR)이 업종 하위권에 머문 상장사를 심사해 주식가치를 30% 이상 높여 과세하는 방안을 내놨지만, 이재명 대통령의 재검토 지시로 대상 기간을 3년으로 줄이고 주식가치 할증 비율을 40%로...

items.title: 공소취소 논란 커지자 다시 조희대 겨눈 與

items.title: 감각 없어지는 건 numb, 그럼 numb-brained의 뜻은?

items.title: 공소청 ‘軍 휴가 미복귀 의혹’ 추미애 아들 수사 재개
items.snippet: 서울동부지방공소청이 최근 추미애 경기지사 아들 서모(32)씨를 출국 금지하고 ‘군 휴가 미복귀 의혹’ 수사를 재개한 것으로 10일 확인됐다. 서씨는 2023년 검찰이 소환을 통보했지만 응하지 않고 튀르키예로 출국했다가 최근 귀국한 것으로 알려졌다. 공소청에 따르면 서씨는 이달 초 인천공항을 통해 귀국했다고 한다. 공소청은 2023년 서씨가 출국한 사실을 확인하고 이듬해 입국 시 통보 및 출국 금지 요청도 법무부에 해 놓았다. 이에 따라 서씨 귀국 사실을 통보받은 공소청이 출국을 금지하고 수사를 다시 시작한 것이다.

items.title: 정치권·민간 뒤흔든 로비 의혹들… 법무부, ‘제도화’ 첫단추 꿸까
items.snippet: 30년 넘게 사업체를 운영해온 A씨는 2022년 한 공기업 납품 비리 사건과 관련해 공기업 간부와 납품업체 관계자 만남을 주선했다는 의혹을 받았다. 그보다 앞서 한 정치자금 위반 사건 재판에선 A씨가 모 정치인에게 금품을 전달했다는 진술이 나왔다. A씨는 두 사건과 관련해 범죄 혐의로 기소되지는 않았다. 미국에선 정관계 인맥을 이용해 행정부나 의회를 상대로 활동하는 사람을 ‘로비스트’라 부른다. 미국에선 로비스트가 합법이다. 그러나 한국에선 A씨처럼 정치인·공직자와 업자를 연결하거나 정치인을 음성적으로 후원하는 사람을 ‘브로커’라 부른다. 합법과 불법 경계를 오간다는 부정적 이미지가 강한 개념이다.

items.title: ‘반짝반짝’ 연말 인천공항 밝히는 전통 그림들
items.snippet: 10일 오후 인천국제공항 제1여객터미널 1층 밀레니엄홀에 연말 장식이 설치됐다. 외국인 관광객이 장식을 구경하며 사진을 찍고 있다. 올해 장식은 새해를 축하하고 재앙을 막기 위해 그렸던 전통 그림 ‘세화(歲畫)’에서 영감을 얻었다. 장식은 내년 1월 31일까지 운영될 예정이다.

items.title: 난방 히트펌프 350만대 보급 추진하는 한국… 가스보일러가 더 저렴
items.snippet: 정부가 난방용 화석연료 사용을 줄이기 위해 히트 펌프 보급을 추진하는 가운데, 한국에선 가스 보일러가 더 경제적이라는 국제에너지기구(IEA)의 분석이 나왔다. 히트 펌프는 전기로 바깥 공기의 열을 실내로 끌어오는 장치다. 가스를 직접 태우지 않아 온실가스 배출을 줄일 수 있다. 기후에너지환경부는 2035년까지 단독주택과 공공·복지 시설 350만곳에 히트 펌프를 보급해 온실가스 518만t을 줄인다는 목표를 세웠다. 이후엔 아파트 등 공동주택에 설치를 의무화하는 방안도 검토 중이다.

items.snippet: 대법원 전원합의체가 오는 19일 한덕수 전 국무총리와 이상민 전 행정안전부 장관의 내란 중요 임무 종사 사건 상고심 심리를 진행한다. 한 전 총리의 구속기간 만료(상고심 6개월) 하루 전이다. 지난 1월 1심 선고와 함께 법정 구속됐던 한 전 총리는 구속 기한인 20일까지 선고가 이뤄지지 않으면 석방될 가능성이 크다.

items.title: 의료분쟁 늘자… 의사·간호사 출신 변호사 모시는 로펌들
items.snippet: 서울 강남구에 있는 A 로펌은 이달 초 의료인 출신 변호사 3명을 한꺼번에 영입했다. 이 중 두 사람은 간호대학을 졸업하고 서울 소재 대학 병원에서 근무한 간호사 출신이고, 다른 한 명은 의학전문대학원을 졸업한 지방 국립대병원 의사 출신이다. B 로펌도 최근 서울 ‘빅(Big)5′ 병원 수술실에서 간호사로 근무했던 신입 변호사를 채용했다. C 로펌은 서울의 한 의대 졸업 후 대학 병원에서 수련 생활을 한 변호사를 올해 영입했다.

items.snippet: 췌장암은 조기 발견이 어렵고 치료도 까다로운 대표적인 암이다. 특히 암세포 주변에 단단한 섬유 조직이 형성돼 면역세포가 암 내부로 침투하기 어렵다. 면역세포가 암을 공격하도록 돕는 면역 항암제가 효과를 내기 어려운 이유다. 이런 췌장암의 방어벽을 허무는 새로운 항암 후보 물질을 개발했다고 미국 예일대와 한국 메드팩토 등 국제 공동연구진이 지난 9일(현지 시각) 국제학술지 ‘캔서 셀(Cancer Cell)’에 발표했다. 이 학술지는 셀(Cell)의 자매지다. 연구진이 췌장암에 걸린 생쥐에게 후보 물질을 투여한 결과, 생쥐의 75%에서 종양이 사라진 것으로 나타났다.

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 10일 이주노동자들의 겨울나기를 돕기 위한 겨울옷 나눔 행사에 동참하겠다고 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 10일 엑스(X·옛 트위터)에 울산에서 이주노동자들에게 겨울옷과 작업복을 전달하는 행사가 열린다는 내용의 기사를 공유하며 “우리 곁 이주노동자들과 따뜻한 겨울을 함께합니다”라는 제목의 글을 올렸다.이 대통령은 “고향과 가족을 떠나 낯선 땅에서 맞는 겨울은 유난히 춥게 느껴지기 마련”이라며 “이주노동자와 함께하는 나눔과 캠페인이 그동안 전국 각지에서 이어져 왔다. 오는 15일에는 울산의 여러 기관과 단체가 힘을 모아 겨울옷과 작업복을 전한다”고 전했다.그러면서 “저도 겨울옷을 보내 작은 정성을 보탤 예정”이라며 “옷 한 벌이 추위를 다 막아 주지는 못하겠지만, 그 안에 담긴 마음만큼은 오랫동안 온기로 남으리라 믿는다”고 덧붙였다.이...

items.title: 李 “부정청약 형사처벌-당첨취소…막대한 재산손실 뒤따를 것”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 10일 정부 합동점검에서 부정청약 의심 사례가 무더기로 적발된 데 대해 “수사결과 부정청약으로 확인되면 형사처벌은 물론 당첨취소 등 막대한 재산상 손해까지 뒤따른다”고 했다.이 대통령은 이날 X(엑스·옛 트위터)에 부정청약 합동점검 결과를 공유하며 이 같이 올렸다. 국토교통부와 국무조정실 부동산감독추진단은 지난해 7월부터 올해 3월까지 분양한 주요 단지 43곳, 2만5000채를 합동점검해 부정청약 의심 사례 354건을 적발했다고 같은 날 밝혔다. 정부는 적발 사례 모두를 수사의뢰할 예정이다.이 대통령은 “향후에도 전수조사는 계속된다”며 “규칙을 어겨 이익볼 수 없고 규칙을 지켜 손해보지 않는 상식적인 나라를 꼭 만들겠다”고 강조했다.

items.title: 한덕수 20일 구속만료로 석방되나…與 “대법, 풀어줄 셈인가”
items.snippet: 내란 중요임무종사 혐의로 항소심에서 징역 15년을 선고받고 수감 중인 한덕수 전 국무총리의 구속기간 만료가 임박한 가운데 더불어민주당이 대법원을 향해 빠른 판결 선고를 요구했다. 구속 기간이 끝나기 전에 선고를 해야 한다는 취지다.이용우 더불어민주당 대변인은 10일 서면브리핑을 통해 “오는 20일이면 한 전 총리의 구속기간이 끝나지만, 대법원은 아직 선고 일정조차 내놓지 않고 있다”며 “대법원은 징역 15년의 내란 중요임무종사자를 풀어줄 셈인가”라고 비판했다.이 대변인은 “대법원은 지난 8월 5일 ‘국민적 관심도가 매우 높고 역사적으로 사법적 평가가 필요하다’며 이 사건을 전원합의체에 회부했으나, 그 뒤 석 달 동안 심리는 단 한 차례 열렸을 뿐”이라며 “대단히 무책임한 행태”라고 꼬집었다.이어 내란특검법 규정을 들어 법원 조치를 압박했다....

items.title: 국힘, 이틀째 청와대 앞 집결…"특검법 거부권 행사해야"
items.snippet: 국민의힘이 오늘(10일) 청와대 앞에서 의원총회를 열고 이재명 대통령에게 조작기소 특검법안에 대해 거부권을 행사할 것을 압박했습니다.특검법안 공포안의 내주 국무회의 상정을 앞두고 지난 주말 대규모 장외 집회에 이어 전날에는 청와대 앞 최고위를 여는 등 대국민 반대 여론전 수위를 연일 높여가는 모습입니다.장동혁 대표는 이날 의총에서 "이번 특검법은 감옥에 있어야 할 이재명을 꺼내기 위한 이재명 탈옥법"이라면서 "이 법에 대해 거부권이 행사되지 않는다면 대한민국 전체가 나서서 거부권을 행사해야 한다"고 목소리를 높였습니다.장 대표는 "다음 총선에서, 다음 대선에서 이재명 정권을 심판해 역사와 법의 심판대에 세울 수 있도록 ..

items.title: 이 대통령 "미 중간선거 이후 변수 대비…금융시장 동요 막아야"
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 오늘(10일) "미국의 중간선거 이후 대외 환경의 여러 가지 변화가 예상된다"며 "관계 부처는 예상되는 다양한 변수를 다각도로 분석해 상황별 대응책을 치밀하게 마련해달라"고 주문했습니다.이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 "대외적 불확실성이 국내 경제에 미칠 부정적 영향을 최소화하는 데 만전을 기해야 한다"며 이같이 밝혔습니다.구체적으로는 "미국과 국제 경제의 상황을 주시하면서 금융 시장이 동요하는 일이 없도록 모니터링을 강화하고 신속한 대응 체계를 잘 갖춰달라"고 주문했습니다.이어 "외풍에 휘둘리지 않으려면 기초 체력을 키우는 일도 꼭 필요하다. 반도체·인공지능 등 핵심 전략산업을 한층 정..

items.snippet: 김지용 중대범죄수사청장이 10일 이재명 대통령이 주재한 국무회의에 참석했다. 지난달 20일부터 중수청장 취임 이후 4주 연속 출석이다. 이 대통령이 앞서 “억지로 올 필요는 없다”고 말했으나, 김 청장은 임명된 이후 열린 네 번의 국무회의에 모두 참석했다.김 청장은 이날 오전 국무회의가 열리기 전 이정현 공소청장 직무대행과 김종철 경찰청장 직무대행을 만나 인사를 나눴다. 김 청장이 국무회의에 처음 참석한 것은 지난달 20일이다. 그는 이 대통령으로부터 같은 달 19일 임명장을 받고 이튿날 곧바로 국무회의에 처음 배석했다. 역대 정부에서는 수사기관의 독립성을 존중해 수사기관장은 국무회의에 배석시키지 않았다. 하지만 이 대통령이 지난해 12월 각 부처 소속의 외청도 국무회의에 참석하라고 지시하면서 검찰총장·경찰청장 직무대행도 배석하기 시작했다....

items.title: 한덕수 석방되나…대법, 구속만기 하루 앞둔 19일 전합 속행기일
items.snippet: 대법원이 다음 주 내란 혐의를 받는 한덕수 전 국무총리와 이상민 전 행정안전부 장관의 전원합의체 사건을 추가 심리하는 기일을 연다.한 전 총리의 구속 만기를 하루 앞두고 선고가 아닌 속행 기일을 잡은 만큼 석방 가능성이 높아졌다.10일 법조계에 따르면 대법원 전원합의체(주심 오경미·김성수 대법관)는 오는 19일 한 전 총리와 이 전 장관의 내란 혐의 상고심 사건 등에 대한 속행기일을 진행한다.한 전 총리는 오는 20일, 이 전 장관은 다음 달 18일 각각 상고심 구속 만기를 앞두고 있다.지난 5일 내란 특검팀(특별검사 조은석)은 두 사람의 구속 만기가 다가오면서 대법원에 신속한 선고를 촉구하는 의견서를 제출한 바 있다.두 사람은 각각 지난 5월 항소심 선고를 받았다. 한 전 총리 징역 15년, 이 전 장관에게는 징역 9년이 선고됐다.대법원은...

items.title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
items.abstract: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. Three platforms show the consequences: a memristor, in which the same voltage writes and reads; a memlumor, in which light both modifies the state and produces the photoluminescence that reports it; and an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), in which the gate writes and the channel reads. items.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gap...

items.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
items.abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

items.title: 피해자가 새 증거 찾아도… 검사 “직접 못 받아” 경찰 “손 떠난 사건”
items.snippet: 사귀던 남성에게 스토킹과 협박을 당한 A씨는 남성이 기소된 후 과거 자신을 협박했던 통화 내역을 추가로 발견했다. A씨는 이 통화 내역을 법정에 추가 증거로 내려 했지만 난관에 부딪쳤다. 예전 같으면 검사에게 내면 됐다. 하지만 지난달 2일 시행된 개정 형사소송법은 검사가 피고인의 유죄 증거를 법원에 내지 못하도록 하고 있다. 경찰에 보완수사를 요구하거나, 피해자가 경찰에 낸 증거를 추송(追送·추후 송부)받아 법원에 내야 한다. A씨 증거를 경찰이 추송해야 해 재판은 2주 이상 지연됐다. A씨 변호인인 곽아량 변호사는 “본래 4주 뒤 재판인데 증거 제출 과정을 거치느라 6주 뒤로 잡았다”며 “검사도 피해자도 모두 답답한 상황”이라고 했다.

items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
items.abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. items.title: 靑 "조작기소 특검법, 다음 주 국무회의 상정 예정"
Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
items.abstract: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. Our results provide a strong incentive for choosing spin qubit initialization schemes which do not rely on coupling to the reservoir in such devices. items.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. Over 10 years of continuous operation under the NEMA Power Index mission profile for variable-load centrifugal systems (pumps, fans), the CSC's higher part-load efficiency translates into a clearly lower life-cycle carbon footpr...

items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an F...

items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. Scaled devices achieved a cutoff frequency ($f_{\mathrm{T}}$) of 35 GHz, a maximum oscillation frequency ($f_{\mathrm{max}}$) of 82 GHz, and an average breakdown field $> 3 \mathrm{MV/cm}$, while maintaining a reasonable current collapse of $\sim 20\%$ under a 40 V drain bias in pinch-off condition. items.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
items.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilizati...

In this work, we employ DFT+U to systematically investigate the thermodynamic stability and magnetic properties of 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ doped with transition metal atoms. We found that the paired dopant configurations are more stable than previously attributed isolated dopants. items.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
items.abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. items.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
items.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. items.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
items.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. items.abstract: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
items.abstract: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. However, no open-source SRAM tool treats topology as an optimizable variable. OpenRAM generates SRAM layouts but performs no optimization, while OpenYield supports high-fidelity evaluation but restricts optimization to scalar sizing of a fixed 6T cell. OpenYieldV2 closes this gap through three integrated contributions. First, a fully parameterized compiler generates complete 6T and 10T SRAM macros with peripheral circuits and replica-bitline self-timing, enabling topology comparison under identical simulation conditions. Second, a few-shot TabPFN surrogate learns topology-dependent PPA responses with limited full-macro SPICE samples. items.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
items.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. items.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
items.abstract: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. FoundaRF establishes a scalable and data-efficient solution for RF/mmWa...

items.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
items.abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU...

items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.abstract: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starti...

items.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. items.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. items.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. items.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
items.abstract: We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window. We design the Micius data pipeline as a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel comprising three stages: knowledge tree construction and expansion, data synthesis, and quality validation with hard-example augmentation. From this data, we train expert models for semiconductor knowledge and reasoning, hardware coding, and semiconductor multimodal understanding, along with agentic experts. Subsequently, we employ Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) to supervise training on sequences generated by Micius itself, thereby integrating the capabilities of these expert models into a unified model. items.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
items.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. items.title: Energy Efficient Near-Threshold Voltage Massive MIMO Computing
items.abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. This work equips conventional massive MIMO algorithms with computational error detection mechanisms, en- abling reliable operation down to near-threshold voltages. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field inse...

items.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
items.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. items.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
items.abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. items.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and ele...

items.abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. This work presents a derivative-free NN training framework employing spectral normalization to naturally smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise. items.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations...

items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window...

items.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. We amortize our generative model by pretraining acro...

items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections,...

items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
items.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physic...

items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.abstract: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. An opt-in, provenance-tracked cost model adds timing fidelity...

items.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
items.abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a...

items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at am...

items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while im...

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sam...

items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding an...

items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors...

items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. items.title: Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning: A Learning-Centered Framework for Designing Immersive Learning Environments
items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. This paper proposes Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning (CSSR) as an integrative framework for understanding how learners establish and use spatial and structural relationships across scales or organizational le...

items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first c...

items.title: PINND: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.
